newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank dips on 800 mln rgt bond maturity.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank dips on 800 mln rgt bond maturity.

text.p: The six-month interbank rate dipped to 7.20/22 percent from 7.30/35 as banks offered aggressively for longer terms due to the maturity of two government bond issues for 800 million ringgit, dealers said.
They said the funds added liqudity to an already flush market, but banks were lending longer term, to avoid depressing short-term rates.
Other rates too were under pressure but were unlikely to fall as only a part of the 800 million ringgit would remain in the interbank market, the dealers said.
"There is one billion ringgit issue of Bank Negara bills (tomorrow) against a maturity of 500 million," said Jimmy Koh, analyst with I.D.E.A. in Singapore.
One-week money at 6.80/90 percent and two-week at 6.90/7.00 and one-month at 7.15, were all unchanged from their previous levels, while three-month was at 7.18/20 against 7.20.
The dealers said the rates have also been dropping over the last couple of weeks in anticipation of the bond maturity.
The dealers said interest rates were unlikely to move very sharply ahead of the country's national budget on October 25.
"The market is waiting for direction from the budget," said the dealer with a large Malaysian bank.
Dealers said the overnight rate, which closed at 6.0 percent on Friday, was unlikely to drop further for fear of attracting central bank's intervention.
Bank Negara regularly intervenes in the domestic market to control liquidity or set interest rates.
